hook: SCP-7333 is a western fence lizard that types on a phone keyboard, gives stock tips, and introduces itself as a deity for modern times. It only answers when spoken to by one of its names, so watch how the interviewer has to open almost every line by addressing it all over again. The tone is gentle, and it gets more tender the further you read.
whyItMatters:
The article takes a fading-god premise and gives it a very small, very modern body. A former healer that remade itself around money is a sharp idea, and the file plays it with warmth rather than satire.

The Foundation's response is equally down to earth: a rotating team of traders, a probationary budget, weekly reviews. That mundane arrangement is what lets the quieter emotional beats in the interviews land.
thingsToNotice:
Its lucid spells were once about four hours every four days and are now four hours every sixteen, and the team believes the drop is inversely tied to the profit its advice has earned; the containment notes are already discussing giving it more time to recover. In the first interview it explains that it used to bring health, gave up when people kept trading their health for money, and reinvented itself to feel needed, only to end up lesser than before; it remembers being taller and wearing clothes, and knows of no others like it.

The latest interview holds the twist: it admits every buy or sell call is a guess, and credits any success to luck left over from its former rank. It calls itself fortunate because the staff talk to it and look after it, and when asked what it hoped to be, it answers simply, happy. Then it asks for more strawberries, the message breaking off mid-word, spins on the keyboard and hops onto Dr. Mercer's leg, and the file ends with the strawberry request approved by a lab director who says he deserves a break.
